title: Map, filter, and reduce differences
description:
Explain the difference between map, filter, and reduce.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as hof_role(name), where name is one of the strings 'map', 'filter', or 'reduce'. Return a tuple (transforms_each_item, filters_by_predicate, produces_single_value) of booleans describing what that higher order function does to an iterable.
examples:
>>> hof_role('map')
(True, False, False)
>>> hof_role('reduce')
(False, False, True)
hints: map, filter, and reduce all take a function and an iterable, but they use the function's result differently.

map applies the function to every item and keeps every result; filter applies a function that returns True/False and keeps only the items that pass; reduce applies the function cumulatively to collapse the iterable into one value.
A dict keyed by the three names, each value the matching 3-tuple, lets you look the answer up by name instead of writing an if/elif chain.
expected_behavior: Returns a 3-tuple of booleans describing whether the named higher order function transforms every item, filters items by a predicate, or reduces the iterable to a single value.

hidden_tests.label: filter selects items with a predicate
reduce produces a single accumulated value

explanation: map transforms every item in the iterable and returns a same-length result. filter keeps only the items for which the given function returns a truthy value, so the result may be shorter. reduce repeatedly combines items with an accumulator until only a single value remains.
